headline: Domestic strength drives profit growth, international lags
summary_short: AutoZone's fiscal Q3 (12 weeks ended May 9, 2026) net sales rose 8.4% y/y to $4.84B and diluted EPS grew to $38.07 from $35.36, as domestic same-store sales rose 4.1% and gross margin slipped 57bp on a non-cash LIFO charge.
summary_long: Net sales rose 8.4% y/y to $4.84B (12 weeks); domestic same-store sales up 4.1%, international up 16.6% as reported (1.6% constant-currency; Mexico and Brazil stayed soft). Operating profit grew 6.6% to $923.8M on opex leverage (33.1% of sales vs 33.3%). Gross margin fell 57bp to 52.2% on a 77bp non-cash LIFO charge, partly offset by other gains. Net income rose 5.4% to $641.5M; diluted EPS rose to $38.07 from $35.36, helped by a lower diluted share count from buybacks. Effective tax rate rose to 21.1% from 19.4%. AutoZone repurchased $586.3M of stock, with $0.8B left under authorization. Cash fell to $253.7M from $268.6M (not explained in the release). Management said pace keeps full-year openings on track for approximately 355-365 stores.

drivers.explanation: Domestic DIY and Commercial strength, expense discipline, and 82 net new stores (on pace for 355-365 for the year) drove the quarter; international stayed soft in Mexico and Brazil despite share gains, per management.

Domestic same-store sales rose 4.1% and international rose 16.6% as reported (1.6% constant-currency) on continued DIY and Commercial growth; total company same-store sales rose 5.5% (3.9% constant-currency).
EPS growth outpaced net income growth as diluted weighted-average shares fell to 16,852K from 17,207K y/y on continued buybacks ($586.3M this quarter).
Net income growth trailed revenue and operating-profit growth because the effective tax rate rose to 21.1% from 19.4% y/y; not addressed in the release's narrative text.
Opex leverage (33.1% of sales vs 33.3% y/y) from strong top-line growth and expense management offset the gross-margin decline, per management commentary.
A 77 basis point net non-cash LIFO impact drove the decline, partially offset by other gross margin improvements, per the release.
